title: Asha and the Weather Mystery
markdown:
Sunlight burst through Asha’s window. A spectacular start! Today was perfect for tide-pool exploring, so Asha bounced out of bed. Then a puff of cool air zipped through her room. Brrr! Her teeth clicked. This was not the warm day promised.

Downstairs, Gran Mae bustled. “Morning, sweet pea,” she chirped, frowning. “Seems those weathermen were dreaming. Such a blustery chill.”

Asha pulled on a jumper. Outside, garden branches danced, looking damp and grey. Then she spotted Drift, Gran Mae’s seal friend, bobbing near the pond. He looked miserable, fur ruffled. Odd. Drift usually basked in sunshine.

“What’s wrong, Drift?” Asha called.

Drift gave a weak bark. “Too cold,” he chattered, whiskers drooping. “Sun’s out, but the wind bites. My flippers are freezing.” He tucked them in, looking awkward.

Asha tilted her head. The sun was high, but the wind was sharp and carried a chill. She remembered her science books: weather. Climate. Big words with big secrets.

“Gran Mae,” she began, mind buzzing, “the forecast said sunshine, but it’s so cold and windy?”

Gran Mae nodded. “It’s been like that for weeks. Peculiar.”

Asha dashed to her desk and pulled out Gran Mae’s Weather Diaries. Page after page of neat handwriting: dates, temperatures, wind directions. Last year’s entries showed warm patterns. Recently? Jumps. Swings. Hot one day, freezing the next. The weather seemed to be playing hopscotch.

“Look.” Asha pointed. “The average temperature over the last ten years keeps going up. That’s our climate, its personality. But today the weather is cold and windy. It’s like my mood.”

Drift poked his head into the kitchen. “Your mood?”

“Weather is like your mood right now. Bouncy or grumpy. It can change so quickly. Climate is like your personality. How you usually are, over a long time. Our planet’s personality, its climate, is getting warmer. We still have days where the mood is cold and windy. That’s the weather. The daily forecast, not the whole story.”

She grabbed chalk and drew a wobbly line on the floor, climbing higher with dips and peaks. “This line is the temperature over many years. See how it’s rising? That’s climate change. The daily ups and downs? That’s weather. This cold wind is just a grumpy-mood day. It doesn’t mean the whole planet is freezing. It’s a temporary feeling.”

Drift blinked, big eyes thoughtful. He nudged the chalk line with his nose. He understood. His shivering was not only a bad day. It was a sign his home, the ocean, felt this change too. The big picture: the climate.

“So,” Gran Mae said, eyes sparkling, “even though it’s cold today, the overall trend is still warmer?”

“Exactly. Our climate is changing, so we get more extreme weather: this cold snap, or hotter heatwaves, or bigger storms. The daily forecast is not the long-term picture. The planet’s personality is shifting.”

Drift nudged Asha’s hand. “Fascinating. I wonder what else the world’s personality is trying to tell us.”

Asha grinned. “Me too. The more we understand, the more we can help.” The blustery morning mystery was solved, and a whole new world of questions buzzed in her head, which was, she thought, a very good way for a morning to keep going.
characters: Asha (an apprentice scientist), Drift (Gran Mae's seal friend), Gran Mae (a weather-diary gran)
